claims.explanation: MK-1775 is a WEE1 kinase inhibitor that abrogates the G2/M DNA-damage checkpoint, causing cells with defective G1 checkpoint control to enter mitosis with unrepaired DNA and die. The strongest predictor of selective killing is loss of p53 function (TP53 mutation/deletion), which is highly enriched in the most-sensitive lines and largely absent from the least-affected lines; additional sensitizing features include oncogenic drivers that increase replication stress (e.g., KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, CCNE1) and loss of DNA-damage-response or chromatin-remodeling genes (ATM, FBXW7, ARID1A, SMARCA4), while intact p53, PTEN, or STK11/LKB1 signaling and low replication stress tend to protect.

features.basis: p53-deficient tumors rely on the G2 checkpoint and are selectively killed by WEE1 inhibition (literature and observed enrichment in sensitive lines)
oncogenic KRAS drives replication stress and dependence on WEE1-mediated checkpoint control
BRAF-mutant tumors show increased replication stress and sensitivity to WEE1 inhibition
EGFR-driven NSCLC lines are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with oncogene-induced replication stress
CCNE1 amplification/high expression causes replication stress and WEE1 dependence
loss of ATM-mediated DNA damage signaling impairs checkpoint recovery and increases reliance on WEE1
FBXW7 loss stabilizes oncoproteins (e.g., cyclin E, MYC) and increases replication stress
ARID1A loss is associated with DNA damage repair defects and sensitivity to checkpoint inhibitors
SMARCA4 loss impairs chromatin-based DNA repair and increases dependence on G2 checkpoint
PTEN loss is enriched in least-affected lines, possibly reflecting intact G1 checkpoint or reduced replication stress
STK11/LKB1 loss is observed in least-affected lines and may reduce sensitivity to WEE1 inhibition
CDKN2A loss impairs G1 checkpoint control, increasing reliance on G2/WEE1
